A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

even in the ionic liquid [bmim+], the cation and anion are strongly interacting with each other, the solute experiences specific interactions with the cation, and this interaction is stronger than its interactions with the anion.
the interactions in the ionic liquids are different from those in other strongly associated solvents.
the ionic liquids are not just a new class of solvents but also a class that can provide new insights into the solute-solvent interaction phenomena.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the solute reorientational dynamics in the ionic liquid are governed by the relative sizes of solute and solvent molecules and not necessarily by the nature of solvent-solute interactions.
even in the case of ionic liquids, where the cations and anions are strongly associated, there are solute-solvent interactions that are not necessarily due to the presence of the ions.
the ionic liquid [bmim+]-[PF6(-)] is not a simple solvent, and its interactions with the solutes are complex.
